open_obligations: Check that the arithmetic tasks are generated the same way in both papers.
Note different models (ChatGPT versus Qwen2.5-7B/Llama3.1-8B) and agent counts (3 versus 5).
Check whether Du et al.'s majority vote uses the same number of samples as debate.
Note that debate rounds differ (Du et al.: 2 rounds; Choi et al.: T = 2, 3, 5).

Note that Choi et al.'s 'in most cases' statement summarises Table 1 across Arithmetics, GSM8K, MMLU Professional Medicine and Formal Logic, HellaSwag, CommonsenseQA and HH-RLHF, plus a Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct run, not arithmetic and GSM8K alone.
Check which of the eight scores belong to the Multi-Agent (Majority) and Multi-Agent (Debate) rows; the reading-order text gives the row labels and the scores apart.
out.other_title: Multiagent debate gives a substantial reasoning boost on arithmetic, grade school math and chess
out.rationale: Du et al.'s results table has the rows Single Agent, Single Agent (Reflection), Multi-Agent (Majority) and Multi-Agent (Debate) and the columns Arithmetic (%), Grade School Math (%) and Chess (∆PS), and the cited lines then list eight scores from 67.0 ± 4.7 to 85.0 ± 3.5, so Du et al. compare multi-agent debate with multi-agent majority voting. Choi, Zhu and Li report that majority voting performs on par with MAD in most cases and say these findings suggest that MAD's effectiveness is largely driven by model ensembling rather than the iterative debate process itself.
out.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: whether multi-agent debate beats majority voting, in Du et al.'s table for arithmetic, grade school math and chess and in Choi, Zhu and Li's own experiments

text: The paper reports that MAD does not reliably surpass the simpler majority-voting strategy, which in most cases performs on par with MAD; with the larger Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, overall MAD performance improves but majority voting still accounts for most of the gains. The authors say these findings suggest that MAD's effectiveness is largely driven by ensembling rather than iterative debate.
title: Majority voting performs on par with multi-agent debate in most cases
